newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S., S.Korea aid to N.Korea said limited for now.
newsitem.headline: U.S., S.Korea aid to N.Korea said limited for now.

text.p: The United States and South Korea do not plan to give large scale food aid to famine-hit North Korea until the communist nation agrees to open peace talks, Japanese officials said on Wednesday.
Briefing reporters on talks in Tokyo involving the two countries and Japan, the officials said Japan did not plan to give any aid at all until ties with North Korea were normalised.
The one-day talks at the Japanese Foreign Ministry focused on food shortages in North Korea and ways to encourage the Stalinist nation to join peace talks.
"We basically agreed it was important to keep a cautious eye on the food situation in North Korea," a foreign ministry official said.

The talks involved Charles Kartman, U.S. deputy assistant secretary of state, Yu Myung-hwan, director-general for North American affairs at the South Korean Foreign Ministry, and his Japanese counterpart, Ryozo Kato.

The United States and South Korea repeated their views that substantial food aid must wait until the North was ready to join the peace talks, although humanitarian assistance would be provided in the meantime, the official said.

Japan reiterated its stance that it was still not ready to offer food aid. Japan has held back aid partly due to anger over charges that North Korea kidnapped a Japanese schoolgirl in 1977 and spirited her to Pyongyang.
Neither the United States nor South Korea pressured Japan to join their efforts to provide food aid, the official said.
"The meeting was not a negotiation, it was not meant to reach any conclusion," he said.
While agreeing that the food shortage in North Korea was serious, the three parties said no one really knew what was happening inside the reclusive state, the official said.

The World Food Programme, a United Nations agency, so far this year has appealed for 200,000 tonnes of food for North Korea, or about $95 million. About $38.6 million of this has been raised. The United States has pledged $25 million and South Korea $6 million.
Peace talks involving the two Koreas, the United States and China are aimed at closing the book on the 1950-53 Korean War, which ended in a now-fraying armistice.
At talks in New York two weeks ago, the United States and South Korea failed to get North Korea to join Korean peninsula peace negotiations.
